title: RawAnalyser: checking raw images in Python

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A camera sensor hands you a raw image. Before anyone makes it pretty, someone has to ask: is it clipped to black or white anywhere?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I never think about that step. Who checks it?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: For one of Antoine's projects, a Python tool called RawAnalyser does. It detects black and white clipping, calculates gamma, and checks flatness with vignette detection, referencing Algolux.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: How do you tell it where to look?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: You give it a folder and a JSON file that marks the region of interest and the gray patches. A small GUI lets you select those on a raw or TIFF file, saves them to that JSON, and keeps watching the raw folder for new files.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So you drop new images in and it checks them.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: That's the idea. There's also a script that inspects a single pixel and uses the Bayer pattern to tell you its color.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: One script converts 20 megapixel images down to 5 megapixels for the OV20880 sensor.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: On GitHub under antoinebou12. The project page lists each script and the libraries it needs.
